abstract: The HIV envelope glycoprotein complex (Env) is the primary target for vaccine development because it elicits neutralizing antibodies. Here, we present a family of HIV Env trimers engineered through strategic circular permutation (CP) of the BG505 and C06980v0c22 strains. We evaluated their quality attributes, including expression yields, oligomeric state, glycosylation profile, antigenicity against broadly neutralizing antibodies (bNAbs), and seroreactivity against plasma from people living with HIV (PLWH). Our results demonstrate that circularly permuted Env constructs maintained native-like trimeric assembly and recognition by benchmark bNAbs targeting major sites of vulnerability. MALDI-TOF MS analysis revealed glycosylation patterns that resemble those of linear Env native trimers, with a shift toward complex-type glycans associated with differential glycan processing. Crucially, the CP constructs exhibited reduced seroreactivity relative to the linear variant (p < 0.05), suggesting possible masking of immunodistracting non-neutralizing epitopes. Together, these results support circular permutation as a viable strategy to refine Env immunogen designs for targeted vaccine development.
